name: Bone resorption
rationale: Mechanical unloading in microgravity is associated with musculoskeletal loss. A sustained decline in strength relative to the personal pattern can justify requesting bone-turnover markers.
evidence: Demonstration pathway. Increased CTX-I during flight has been described in NASA literature; using grip strength as a trigger is a design hypothesis that needs validation.

name: Kidney stone risk
rationale: Bone resorption releases calcium that is excreted in urine. A change in CTX-I can justify reviewing urinary calcium and kidney function.
evidence: Design hypothesis. No clinically validated thresholds in this demo.

name: Inflammation or overtraining
planned_signals: continuous cortisol in sweat or interstitial fluid (experimental)
rationale: Combined changes in temperature, heart rate variability, sleep, or cortisol may justify an inflammatory lab panel.
evidence: Design hypothesis. Continuous lactate and cortisol sensors are not validated for mission use.

name: Cardiovascular or orthostatic changes
rationale: A sustained change in heart rate or HRV can justify a blood pressure measurement and further assessment.
evidence: Design hypothesis. Interpretation requires a reviewed medical protocol.
